SPRINT 66 (V0.29.20) -- US-496 (S3 Pi-local cards live + honest-gray) DONE, 3/7.
THE HEADLINE LESSON: A HIDE IS NOT A FREE STYLING CHANGE -- IT CHANGES THE GEOMETRY. AC-3 asks for one card to be hidden rather than grayed; because #track is a flex row of full-width cards and US-495's [hidden] guard genuinely removes the element, a hidden card takes NO SLOT. So translateX, the page dots, the swipe, and the "where do I land if the card I am on vanishes" recovery all had to start counting VISIBLE cards (new pure visualPosition / nextVisibleIndex / nearestVisibleIndex; goTo() now refuses a hidden target; a hidden card owns no dot, because a dot navigating nowhere is the same dead affordance as the card behind it). If you gate another card that math is already there -- but the FEEL of it is an on-Pi check, not a unit test.
AND THE FRAGILITY THAT CAME WITH IT: the whole gate rests on `hidden` removing the card from flow, which only works because US-495's guard wins on IMPORTANCE. Adding `!important` to .card or .dot's `display` would tie importance, hand the win to the later same-specificity selector, and silently restore a gated card to the track -- the US-495 defect again, from a one-word edit. There is now a test forbidding it. NOTE for US-499/S6: the US-495 guard test only enumerates elements the MARKUP ships `hidden`; the page dots are JS-CREATED, so the real cascade over them is still unexercised. That, plus the visible-index geometry, is the highest-value thing S6 can render for real.
GRAY vs HIDDEN IS A REAL DISTINCTION, worth carrying: gray says "this instrument is BROKEN"; hidden says "it does not APPLY right now". On a bench with no car, a grayed fuel-trim card is a false fault report. Hence the gate demands an EXPLICIT source.obd.available === true -- deliberately STRICTER than sourceUnavailable(), whose absent-source-block-means-available default is right for "should I gray this tile?" and WRONG for "should I reveal a vehicle card?". THIS SPRINT HAS NOW FOUND THE SAME UNDERLYING BUG THREE STORIES RUNNING (US-492 guard-down banner, US-494 OBD_STARTING, US-496 here): a reading NOT TAKEN rendered as a confident state. Treat `X or <plausible-default>` and any absent-means-fine default as a code smell on sight, and ask whether the consumer needs "gray it" or "reveal it" semantics -- they need OPPOSITE defaults.
JUDGEMENT CALL, PM/ATLAS PLEASE CONFIRM: AC-3 names a "Live Engine Data card" that does not exist yet (Atlas: Slice 2), so I built the MECHANISM and applied it to LTFT rather than DELETING that card. Atlas's design says "remove from carousel now"; the story's conditionalOutcome says "leave it out of the always-present set ... do not fake it". Gating satisfies both readings, keeps code Slice 2 may revive, and exercises the seam Live Engine Data will inherit. Bench observable is identical to the AC (no vehicle card).
LIGHT CARD (it did not exist -- this was the real build). A pure consumer of the SAME states/light file that drives the auto-dim, so I made the tick resolve ONE clock for both the card's freshness verdict and the applied brightness -- otherwise card and screen could disagree by a poll interval about whether the feed is stale. Also DEDUPED the fetch (the tick already fetched `light` for brightness; a naive card would poll the same file twice per tick at 4 Hz). TWO tiles, and THE OMISSION IS THE DESIGN: AMBIENT (reading + read age) and CONDITION (DARK/DIM/DAYLIGHT). I did NOT add the screen-brightness percent, though it was the obvious third tile -- a live STOP holds the surface at FULL regardless of lux (US-484-b ch.4), so a lux-derived percent would contradict the actual screen exactly when it matters most. CONDITION resolves against the SAME injected luxMin/luxFull: a NAME for existing grounded thresholds, never a third set of numbers (proven with a config override, so the values are read, not baked in). The three gray REASONS are distinct on purpose -- "no reading ever arrived" vs "readings stopped arriving" vs "undated" are different faults and the operator needs to know which. No config change needed: pi.sensors.light.enabled was already true (V0.29.15).
DTC NO-DATA was NARROWER than it looks: empty-available ALREADY rendered a calm gray "No stored codes", and the phantom red was S2's CSS bug. The only real gap was an ABSENT state rendering the bare word "unavailable" -> added noDataView(name) for the two cards whose SILENCE is dangerous to misread (dtc: "no data -- codes not read", never an all-clear; light: "no data -- light feed absent", not "dark"). Deliberately NOT applied to the other three (scope fence). Kept alertsCardView(null) === null -- tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py:1017 pins it, and the SHELL is the right single place to decide absence for every card.
GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 282 passed -- tests/ui 233 (33 new) + test_dashboard_kit 49; ruff clean on both touched Python files; carousel.js parses under node (every probe-driven test requires the module). Bumped test_dashboard_kit's card-slot count 4 -> 5. NO Python SOURCE changed, so tests/pi cannot have regressed. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64/65/66): make, black, mypy absent on this Windows box -- PM please run mypy at integration. FIDELITY LIMIT stated plainly: the DOM wiring is pinned by asserting on the SHIPPED tick/render/move BODIES, which is source-text evidence, not a render.
ARCHITECTURE DoD met in-sprint (Rule 10): specs/architecture.md F-092 gained a "Card model: always-present vs vehicle-gated" section (two-tier table, gray-vs-hidden, strict-gate rationale, visible-card geometry, per-card absent-state messages, and the Light card contract incl. why brightness is not on it).
ON-PI GATE OWED (AC-5): deploy, then bench with NO car -- (a) swipe: Standby / System Status / Battery / LIGHT / Alerts, NO LTFT card and NO sixth dot; (b) Light shows a real changing lux (cover the TSL2591 @0x29) with CONDITION tracking; (c) Alerts reads gray "no data" or "No stored codes", NOTHING red; (d) COUNT THE DOTS against the visible cards -- that is the one thing the new geometry could get wrong in a way no unit test sees. Later, with the car: LTFT should APPEAR and read "unavailable" (orphaned emitter -- honest, Slice 2's item, NOT a regression).
NEXT UP is US-478 (S4-emitter IMU bring-up) but it is HARDWARE-GATED: its own AC records 2026-07-27 that the bus shows only 0x29 + 0x36, no 0x69 -- blocked on AI-005 (CIO wires the board). Its conditionalOutcome makes shipping the enable+bridge CODE with validation deferred a PM CALL AT DISPATCH. US-499 (S6 render-regression) is fully unblocked and is now the highest-value story left -- S1/S2/S3 have every one of them ended with an owed on-Pi render check. Carried debt unchanged: TD-067, TD-068.
